### Summary

A regression test is a test that was written to fail on a defect before the defect was fixed. Its value is in
that history: it fails on the commit it was written against (RED), it passes on the fix (GREEN), and from then on
it keeps the defect from coming back. The history is not visible in the test's body, and most of the tests below
do not name the defect they pin. This section is that record, for the regression tests of the closing round: for
each one, what it checks and the RED and fix commits it came from. Every commit named here is on the history of
the code pin.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Record, for each regression test of the closing round, the defect it pins and the commits that
made it RED and then GREEN.

**Data.** Reads the test files and the commit history at the pin; writes nothing.

**Placement.** A record; the tests themselves run in ctest with the rest of the suite.

**Activation.** None: every row is a registered ctest entry, run by `ctest -R <name>`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Every RED and fix commit is an ancestor of the pin, and every named test case exists at
the pin. The record covers the closing round; earlier regression tests are listed in the chapters that own
their code.

**Evidence.** The tests of @tbl-ch16-regressions; their tolerances are in @tbl-ch16-regressions-tests.
:::

Local symbols of this section: none.

### Derivation

None: a record. The one rule it follows is the order of a regression fix: the test is committed first and fails
on the code of its commit (RED), and the fix commit makes it pass without changing the test's assertion
(GREEN). Where a test case arrived in the same commit as its fix, the row says so instead of naming a RED commit.

### Numerical method

Each row was built the same way: find the commit that added the test case (`git log --diff-filter=A` for a new
file, `git show` for a case added to an existing file), read its message for the RED marker, find the commits
after it that change the code the test exercises, and check with `git merge-base --is-ancestor` that each is on
the history of the pin. The commits are given in each row's footnote; the body of a chapter carries no commit
sha.

| test (ctest name) | case | what it pins |
|---|---|---|
| `test_graph_stretched_x1_python` | `main` | a stretched cubed sphere captures and equals eager; the stretched $x_1$ reference rows are built on the grid's device, so no host-to-device copy runs inside a capture[^ch16-reg-stretched] |
| `test_graph_monitor_amounts.release` | `GraphSaveList.user_forcing_graph_books_wall_rates_like_eager` | under a user forcing, a cuda-graph block books the wall rates and count masks as eager does, from fixed device storage in the stage's push order[^ch16-reg-monitor] |
| `test_flux_register.release` | `FluxRegister.wall_prescription_books_in_float32_on_the_device` | the wall weights' scalar operands are in the wide dtype on the device[^ch16-reg-f32] |
| `test_flux_register.release` | `FluxRegister.the_wall_batch_books_with_the_rebuilt_weights` | a wall-batch slot is tied to the weights it was registered with[^ch16-reg-weights] |
| `test_flux_register.release` | `FluxRegister.the_solid_mask_frees_the_x1_wall_rows_too` | the solid-mask prescription frees the $x_1$ wall rows too[^ch16-reg-solid] |
| `test_default_execution_python` | `main` | `integration/execution` defaults to cuda-graph on CUDA; split cubed-sphere panels capture by default[^ch16-reg-default] |
| `test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager_python` | `main` | the graph path's EfStatus meters, the conversion-trips slot among them, match eager across capture warm-ups[^ch16-reg-meters] |
| `test_flux_positivity_carry.release` | `flux_positivity.a_carry_without_settling_marks_the_direction` | a positivity carry without a settling part marks its direction for the post-implicit apply[^ch16-reg-carry] |
| `test_prescribed_after_sources.release` | `FluxRegister.a_source_post_on_the_walls_does_not_reach_du`, `FluxRegister.a_prescribed_wall_temperature_conducts_in_a_full_step` | the prescribed faces are prescribed again after the sources' posts; a wall that prescribes a temperature keeps its energy row[^ch16-reg-sources] |
| `test_diffusion.release` | `DeviceTest.disabled_direction_register_carries_the_diffusion_energy` | with a flux direction off, the diffusion's energy rows still go through the register[^ch16-reg-diffusion] |
| `test_implicit_register_x1_off_python` | `main` | with the $x_1$ flux off, the implicit solve books its transfers in the register[^ch16-reg-implicit] |
| `test_graph_mesh_many_blocks_python` | `main` | a Mesh of many blocks captures and equals eager; a capture owns its stream[^ch16-reg-many] |
| `test_mesh_worker_streams.release` | `MeshWorkerStreams.no_two_blocks_share_a_stream` | the block worker pool creates its own streams[^ch16-reg-streams] |
| `test_mesh_block_job_failure_python` | `main` | a block job that fails on one block of a Mesh ends the Mesh's same-process waits instead of hanging it[^ch16-reg-failure] |
| `test_seam_rotation_cache_python` | `main` | the panel-seam rotation operands are built once per grid[^ch16-reg-rotation] |
| `test_mesh_disagree.release` | `MeshDisagree.*` | a Mesh whose blocks disagree on capture runs eager, in bounded time; strict refuses it[^ch16-reg-disagree] |

### Code

The tests are cited by file: `test_graph_stretched_x1.py` ({{< code tests/test_graph_stretched_x1.py >}}),
`test_graph_monitor_amounts.cpp` ({{< code tests/test_graph_monitor_amounts.cpp >}}), `test_flux_register.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_flux_register.cpp >}}), `test_default_execution.py`
({{< code tests/test_default_execution.py >}}), `test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager.py`
({{< code tests/test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager.py >}}), `test_flux_positivity_carry.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_flux_positivity_carry.cpp >}}), `test_prescribed_after_sources.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_prescribed_after_sources.cpp >}}), `test_diffusion.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp >}}), `test_implicit_register_x1_off.py`
({{< code tests/test_implicit_register_x1_off.py >}}), `test_graph_mesh_many_blocks.py`
({{< code tests/test_graph_mesh_many_blocks.py >}}), `test_mesh_worker_streams.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_mesh_worker_streams.cpp >}}), `test_mesh_block_job_failure.py`
({{< code tests/test_mesh_block_job_failure.py >}}), `test_seam_rotation_cache.py`
({{< code tests/test_seam_rotation_cache.py >}}) and `test_mesh_disagree.cpp`
({{< code tests/test_mesh_disagree.cpp >}}); their registrations are in {{< code tests/CMakeLists.txt >}}.

**What is refused, and why.** Not applicable: a record refuses nothing. The graph tests among the rows end with
the skip code when the build has no CUDA, and ctest then reports them skipped, not passed.

### Tests

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_graph_stretched_x1_python` | every block's state after every step, graph against eager | `torch.equal` (bitwise); its `rtol=1.e-13` is the tolerance of the column solve that builds the initial state, not of a comparison | {{< code tests/test_graph_stretched_x1.py >}} |
| `test_graph_monitor_amounts.release` | the monitor's amounts, graph against eager | `torch::equal` (bitwise), 7 calls | {{< code tests/test_graph_monitor_amounts.cpp >}} |
| `test_flux_register.release` | the register's booked and applied amounts | `torch::equal` (bitwise), 29 calls; one `allclose` with `rtol=0., atol=0.` | {{< code tests/test_flux_register.cpp >}} |
| `test_default_execution_python` | the default path against explicit eager | `torch.equal` (bitwise), 2 calls | {{< code tests/test_default_execution.py >}} |
| `test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager_python` | the EfStatus meters, graph against eager | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_graph_positivity_meters_match_eager.py >}} |
| `test_flux_positivity_carry.release` | the carried energy and momentum of withheld mass | `torch::equal` (bitwise), 4 calls; `EXPECT_NEAR` with `tol = 1e-12` times the larger magnitude, and `0.` | {{< code tests/test_flux_positivity_carry.cpp >}} |
| `test_prescribed_after_sources.release` | the energy change against the booked flux | `EXPECT_NEAR` with `tol = 1e-12` times the cell energy sum; `EXPECT_LT(tol0, ...)` | {{< code tests/test_prescribed_after_sources.cpp >}} |
| `test_diffusion.release` | the diffusion's heat and the register's energy rows | `EXPECT_NEAR` and `allclose`, case by case; the row's case is read in the file | {{< code tests/test_diffusion.cpp >}} |
| `test_implicit_register_x1_off_python` | the booked transfers with the $x_1$ flux off | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_implicit_register_x1_off.py >}} |
| `test_graph_mesh_many_blocks_python` | a Mesh of many blocks, graph against eager | `torch.equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_graph_mesh_many_blocks.py >}} |
| `test_mesh_worker_streams.release` | the worker streams are distinct | pass/fail checks only | {{< code tests/test_mesh_worker_streams.cpp >}} |
| `test_mesh_block_job_failure_python` | a 24-block Mesh whose capture or eager step runs out of device memory on some blocks returns one error to the caller and does not hang (each arm runs in a child process under a timeout) | pass/fail checks only | {{< code tests/test_mesh_block_job_failure.py >}} |
| `test_seam_rotation_cache_python` | after a warm step no rotation kernel is launched again; after a device move, a storage swap at the same address or a dtype move, the operands are rebuilt and the Mesh equals a fresh one | `torch.equal` (bitwise), 3 calls; a kernel count from the profiler |  {{< code tests/test_seam_rotation_cache.py >}} |
| `test_mesh_disagree.release` | the disagreeing Mesh against eager | `torch::equal` (bitwise) | {{< code tests/test_mesh_disagree.cpp >}} |

: Tests of the regression record and the tolerance each uses. {#tbl-ch16-regressions-tests}

The call counts are `grep -cE 'torch(::|\.)equal'` over each test file at the pin.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The record covers the regression tests of the closing round only; a regression test written earlier is cited
  in the chapter that owns its code, without its commits.
- A row's "what it pins" is read from the RED and fix commits' messages and the test; it is not rerun on the RED
  commit here.
- Where a row has two fixes, the second refined the first; both are needed at the pin.
:::
